scenes.title: Gravity's Ocean Embrace
scenes.narration: Tides are the rhythmic rise and fall of ocean waters, primarily driven by the powerful gravitational pull of the Moon. This force creates a noticeable bulge in the ocean, even though the Moon is 384,400 km away.

scenes.title: Two Bulges, Two High Tides
scenes.narration: The Moon's gravity pulls water towards it, creating a high tide bulge on the near side. Simultaneously, inertial forces cause a second bulge on the far side, resulting in two high tides daily.

scenes.title: Earth's Rotation & Tides
scenes.narration: As Earth rotates through these two bulges over a 24-hour period, any given location experiences two high tides and two low tides. This cycle is slightly longer than 24 hours due to the Moon's orbit.

scenes.title: Sun's Influence: Spring & Neap Tides
scenes.narration: The Sun's gravity also affects tides; when the Sun, Moon, and Earth align (new/full moon), their combined pull creates stronger spring tides. When they are at right angles (quarter moons), weaker neap tides occur.

scenes.title: Predictable Rhythms, Global Impact
scenes.narration: The predictable rhythm of tides is crucial for navigation, marine ecosystems, and renewable energy. Understanding these gravitational forces allows us to harness their power and navigate coastal waters safely.
